### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | None on the guidelines page; Sage's publisher-wide policy applies |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional: disclosure for generative uses, no prior permission |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | Sage policy (live page returns 403; read from a Wayback snapshot dated 2026-11-15): assistive AI that improves language, grammar or structure needs no disclosure; generative use that produces text, references, images or other content affecting methodology, analysis, results or conclusions must be disclosed at submission, in the Methods or Acknowledgements. Listed disclosed-use examples: literature review help, translation, code, data visualisation, reference compilation. Inappropriate uses include fabricated references, generated data, AI "interviews" in place of participants, and undisclosed use; submissions are not rejected solely for disclosed use, but undisclosed inappropriate use can lead to rejection at any stage. Reviewers must not upload manuscripts to generative tools; editors must not use them for decision letters or summaries of unpublished work. Correction: the previous version of this entry was in Chinese and relied on a page it could not fully read; the facts here come from the archived page |
| **Source URL** | https://www.sagepub.com/journals/publication-ethics-policies/artificial-intelligence-policy |

### Orientation

> Keyword counts below are from Crossref records for ISSN 0048-3931 and 1552-7441, journal articles from 2021-01 to 2026-11-23: 170 articles, of which 138 (81%) carry a deposited abstract, retrieved 2026-11-23. Keywords were matched locally in title plus abstract, shares are of the 138 with abstracts, and all counts are lower bounds. OpenAlex `works` queries were not available (daily budget exhausted), so Crossref was used.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Philosophical argument is the main mode: "argu*" in 70 of 138 abstracts (50.7%), "philosoph*" 36 (26.1%), "conceptual" 11 (8.0%). Empirical material is present but smaller: "empirical" 16 (11.6%), "case study" 14 (10.1%), "experiment*" 3 (2.2%) |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Few social-science method terms: "statistic/regression/quantitative" 5 (3.6%), "qualitative" 4 (2.9%), "survey/questionnaire" 2 (1.4%), "ethnograph*" 2 (1.4%), "interview" 0; "model*" appears in 28 (20.3%), often in the sense of theoretical or economic models |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | The aims page says each issue presents scholars from anthropology, communications, economics, history, linguistics, philosophy, psychology and sociology (https://journals.sagepub.com/aims-scope/pos, Wayback snapshot 2022-01-19). Counts: "econom*" 19 (13.8%), "psycholog*" 13 (9.4%), "politic*" 12 (8.7%), "sociolog*" 11 (8.0%), "anthropolog*" 8 (5.8%) |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** the editor-run page describes an international journal publishing articles, discussions, symposia, literature surveys, translations and review symposia for philosophers concerned with the social sciences and for social scientists concerned with their philosophical foundations, favouring no school, party or style (https://poss.info.yorku.ca, retrieved 2026-11-23). Recent Crossref titles (2026) include "Analogy as Conceptual Infrastructure: Rethinking the Ontology and Methodology of Economics" (DOI 10.1177/00483931261509236), "Social Normativity Without Realism: A Fictionalist Challenge" (10.1177/00483931261505199), "Measurement and Instrument Development in the Human Sciences" (10.1177/00483931261483173) and "Social Explanations: A New Approach" (10.1177/00483931261505200).

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** philosophical analysis of social-science concepts and methods (explanation, measurement, models, rationality); social ontology; philosophy of economics; history of theories and concepts; replies and symposia.

## Soft Metadata

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

- Editorial statement: the journal has an "open editorial policy": no school, party or style of philosophy of the social sciences is favoured and debate between schools is encouraged (https://journals.sagepub.com/aims-scope/pos, Wayback snapshot 2022-01-19; the same wording appears on https://poss.info.yorku.ca, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- Topics named in the aims page: ethnomethodology, evolution, Marxism, phenomenology, postmodernism, rationality, relativism, scientific methods and textual interpretations; central issues include explaining, theorising and testing, individualism versus holism, the nature of rationality and the history of theories and concepts.
- Terms in titles/abstracts of 138 articles with abstracts, 2021-2026 (Crossref, retrieved 2026-11-23): social ontology, social kinds, social construction or collective intentionality 22 (15.9%); rationality or rational choice 11 (8.0%); Popper 9 (6.5%); naturalis* 7 (5.1%); individualism or holism 6 (4.3%); interpretive or hermeneutic 6 (4.3%); pragmati* 5 (3.6%); Weber 4 (2.9%); phenomenolog* 2 (1.4%); Marx* 1 (0.7%); critical realis* 1 (0.7%); Wittgenstein or Winch 1 (0.7%).
- OpenAlex topics (spine, 2026-07-13): Contemporary Sociological Theory and Practice 247, Economic Theory and Institutions 226, Critical Realism in Sociology 178, Political Economy and Marxism 133 topic assignments.
- Reading of the counts: the 2021-2026 abstracts lean toward analytic philosophy of science and social ontology, with Popperian and naturalistic strands visible and Marxist and critical-realist labels rare in abstracts, even though OpenAlex assigns such topics to older content. This describes what is published, not editors' politics.

### Framing Requirements

- Mandatory framing: no framing rule is stated in the guide for authors; the editor-run page defines scope as philosophical issues of interest both to philosophers concerned with the social sciences and to social scientists concerned with their foundations (https://poss.info.yorku.ca, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- Article types: articles, discussions, symposia, literature surveys, translations and review symposia (same URL); review essays and reviews are normally commissioned (guide, https://sage.cnpereading.com/storage/ext/submission-guidelines/page/author-instructions_POS.html, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- Format of the package: abstract of 100 words or less and four or five keywords for articles, plus a short biographical note on research areas and recent publications (same guide).
- Replies and symposia are part of the output: 18 of 170 Crossref titles contain "reply", "response" or "comment" (own count, retrieved 2026-11-23), e.g. "The Analytic Cart Before the Ontological Horse: A Response to Michell's ..." (DOI 10.1177/00483931261504479).
- Consequence of ignoring the scope: no desk-reject statement exists on the pages read.

### Methodological Preferences

Scoring rule (this pass's own convention, not the journal's): hits divided by the 138 articles with abstracts, 2021-2026; 0 gives 0, under 1% gives 1, 1-5% gives 2, over 5% gives 3. Scores of 4-5 need a cited editorial statement and none was found. Source: Crossref titles/abstracts for ISSN 0048-3931, retrieved 2026-11-23; counts are lower bounds.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Philosophical argument / conceptual analysis | 3 | "argu*" 70 articles (50.7%), "philosoph*" 36 (26.1%), "conceptual" 11 (8.0%); capped at 3 by rule though clearly the dominant mode |
| Theoretical or formal modelling | 3 | "model*" 28 articles (20.3%); the stem covers conceptual discussion of models as well as modelling work, so this overstates modelling |
| Historical / history of ideas | 3 | "histor*" 11 articles (8.0%) |
| Case studies | 3 | "case stud*" 14 articles (10.1%); in philosophy abstracts this often means an illustrative case |
| Empirical studies (general) | 3 | "empirical" 16 articles (11.6%) |
| Quantitative / statistical | 2 | "statistic, regression, quantitative" 5 articles (3.6%) |
| Qualitative methods | 2 | "qualitative" 4 articles (2.9%) |
| Survey / questionnaire | 2 | 2 articles (1.4%) |
| Ethnography | 2 | 2 articles (1.4%) |
| Behavioural experiments | 2 | "experiment*" 3 articles (2.2%) |
| Interviews | 0 | 0 articles in 138 |
| Simulation / agent-based | 0 | 0 articles in 138 |

### Voice & Style

- Stated style rules: American spelling, Webster's Ninth Collegiate Dictionary as authority, dates fully spelled out, contractions to be avoided, Chicago "B" references, double-spaced text; abstract 100 words or less (guide, https://sage.cnpereading.com/storage/ext/submission-guidelines/page/author-instructions_POS.html, retrieved 2026-11-23). The guide has older passages and may be stale.
- Authorship pattern: 147 of 167 articles with author data (88%) have a single author (Crossref, own count, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- First-person use in titles/abstracts (138 articles with abstracts, Crossref, retrieved 2026-11-23): "I" in 53 (38.4%), "we" in 30 (21.7%), "my" or "our" in 21 (15.2%); "this paper/article/essay" in 66 (47.8%). Examples: "In this paper I make two contributions" (DOI 10.1177/00483931261505203), "I challenge forms of social normativism" (10.1177/00483931261505199).
- Recent openings sampled (DOIs): 10.1177/00483931261509236 opens with a claim about analogy in economics; 10.1177/00483931261483173 opens with a question ("Can measurement provide an independent source of evidence in the human sciences?"); 10.1177/00483931261505200 opens by defining the view proposed; 10.1177/00483931261489617 opens "This article examines the tension..."; 10.1177/00483931261504479 is a response that states three concerns; 10.1177/00483931261510390 opens by naming the book discussed.

### Practical Concerns

- Submission: through ScholarOne at the journal's manuscript-site path (https://sage.cnpereading.com/storage/ext/submission-guidelines/page/author-instructions_POS.html, retrieved 2026-11-23); books for review go to the Managing Editor.
- Copyright permission: quotations aggregating 300 words or more from a single work require the holder's permission, obtained by the author (same guide).
- Preprints: allowed with notice to the Editorial Office and the DOI entered at submission; no update posted during review; link to the final version added after acceptance (same guide).
- OA and charges: Sage Choice gold OA for a publication fee, peer review unchanged (same guide); the journal homepage lists both open-access and restricted-access articles (Wayback snapshot 2025-06-29).
- AI: disclosure of generative uses per Sage policy (URL in the AI Policy table, Wayback snapshot 2026-11-15).
- Publication ethics: the homepage states the journal is a member of the Committee on Publication Ethics (https://journals.sagepub.com/home/POS, Wayback snapshot 2025-06-29).
- IRB or ethics-approval rule, data-availability statement, authorship criteria, anonymisation and independent-scholar rules: none stated in the guide text (own text search, 2026-11-23).

## Strategic Notes

> Every statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Judgements about the journal's culture are not made because the evidence for them is absent.

### Hard Blockers

- Over-length abstract: the guide asks for 100 words or less for articles (Format table).
- Generative AI use that affects method, analysis or conclusions without disclosure, or fabricated references and AI-generated "interviews" (AI Policy table).
- Posting an updated preprint version while the paper is under review (Preprint Policy table).
- Quotation of 300 words or more from one work without the holder's permission (Format table).

### Soft Tax

- House style: Chicago "B" references, American spelling, no contractions, fully spelled-out dates, double-spaced final copy (Voice & Style).
- Timeline: the only figure is the journal's own norm of 2 to 4 months for refereeing; no observed times exist (Review Cycle Time).
- Unknown review model: the guide does not say whether review is blind, so anonymisation requirements need checking in the submission system (Peer Review table).
- OA cost is not recorded: Sage Choice fee not read (Open Access table).

### Best Suited For

- Single-author argumentative papers in philosophy of the social sciences: 88% of articles are single-authored and "argu*" appears in 50.7% of abstracts (Orientation, Voice & Style).
- Papers on social ontology, social kinds and social explanation: 22 articles (15.9%) (Epistemological Leanings).
- Papers on philosophy of economics, measurement and models: "econom*" 13.8%, "model*" 20.3% (Orientation).
- Replies and discussion pieces responding to published work: 18 of 170 titles (Framing Requirements).

### Not Recommended For

- Papers whose main contribution is original interview, survey or ethnographic data: "interview" 0, "survey" 1.4%, "ethnograph*" 1.4% of abstracts (Methodological Preferences); this is rarity, not a stated exclusion.
- Simulation or agent-based modelling papers: 0 articles in 138 (Methodological Preferences).
- Papers centred on religion: 0 articles (Sensitive Topics); rarity, not a stated exclusion.
